newsitem.title: USA: DLJ Merchant to have 79 pct stake in Duane Reade.
newsitem.headline: DLJ Merchant to have 79 pct stake in Duane Reade.

text.p: DLJ Merchant Banking Partners II is acquiring about 79 percent of Duane Reade Holding Corp, Duane Reade chairman and chief executive officer Anthony Cuti told Reuters.

Earlier, Duane Reade said in a statement that DLJ Merchant, an affiliate of Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette, would become the majority shareholder in Manhattan drug store chain Duane Reade in a $350 million recapitalization.
Cuti on Friday said DLJ Merchant Banking Partners II is buying 90 percent of Bain Capital's stake in Duane Reade and buying out all other holders except management.
Cuti told Reuters that currently Bain Capital owns 68.5 percent of the company, other investors hold 17.5 percent, management holds 11.4 percent and the remainder is held by ex-employees.
"When the smoke clears, management will own 11 percent of the company, Bain will have 10 percent and DLJ Merchant Banking will have the rest," Cuti said.

The transaction is subject to terms and conditions customary in transactions of this type, including expiration of applicable waiting periods under the Hart-Scott-Rodino Antitrust Improvements Act of 1976, and will be treated as a recapitalization for accounting purposes, Duane Reade said.
Headquartered in Manhattan, Duane Reade is the largest drug store chain in Manhattan with more than 60 stores and sales in 1996 of approximately $383 million.
Cuti said that the company would be "more aggressive" in its expansion but he declined to provide more details.
